edge_skill.DEG_in: When interpreting DEG_in edges, treat endocrine hormone DE signal detected in non-cognate cell types (e.g., INS outside beta, GCG not in alpha) as a high-risk technical artefact unless validated by additional evidence. Human islet droplet scRNA-seq is known to have ambient/cell-free hormone RNA contamination and “conflicted hormone expression” attributable to ambient mRNA/lysis; this can create spurious DEGs and distort cluster/pseudobulk means. Therefore, do NOT state “Alpha cells express INS” as a biological fact; instead phrase as: “INS signal in α-cells may reflect ambient RNA / doublets / mixed-hormone artefacts”.
edge_skill.T1D_DEG_in: Interpret T1D_DEG_in as RNA differential expression associated with Type 1 Diabetes in a specific anatomical structure or cell type. Report UpOrDownRegulation, Log2FoldChange, SE_of_Log2FoldChange, P_value, Adjusted_P_value, data_version, and data_source when present. Treat endocrine hormone DE signal in non-cognate cell types as high-risk technical artefact unless validated; do not state non-cognate hormone expression as biological fact. Prefer wording such as: signal may reflect ambient RNA, doublets, mixed-hormone artefacts, donor imbalance, or pseudobulk/modeling effects.
edge_skill.expression_level_in: Current PanKgraph expression data was not nromalized across cell types so do not make cross cell type expression level comparison. When interpreting expression_level_in edges, treat the reported summary statistics as potentially inflated for strong/ dominant genes across multiple cell types. In droplet-based islet data, ambient RNA (INS/GCG-rich background) and mixed/doublet contamination can systematically elevate apparent hormone expression in non-cognate populations because hormone transcripts can dominate libraries. Therefore, if hormone genes show measurable signal in non-cognate type (e.g., INS in α cells), annotate it as “potential ambient/contamination signal” unless there is strong literature support. Prefer wording such as: “INS signal detected in α-cell aggregates may be driven by ambient hormone RNA; avoid interpreting this as true α-cell transcription without additional validation.” Conversely, avoid absolute “not expressed” claims for low/undetected genes. Pseudobulk aggregation, filtering thresholds, donor imbalance, and normalization choices can reduce sensitivity and mask low-level expression. Check literature for more info. Prefer cautious phrasing like: No robust signal detected under the current pseudobulk/thresholding settings.
edge_skill.gene_detected_in: Interpret gene_detected_in as pseudobulk scRNA-seq detection support for a gene in an anatomical structure or cell type, not proof of cell-type-specific expression. Report condition, cell_type, n_donors, total_cells, median_donor_logCPM, median_pct_cells_expressing, expression_call, confidence_label, detection_rule, thresholds, data_version, and data_source when present. Do not compare raw expression values across cell types as normalized biological abundance; flag possible ambient RNA, doublets, donor imbalance, thresholding, and pseudobulk aggregation effects. Avoid absolute absence claims when a gene is not detected.
edge_skill.gene_enriched_in: Interpret gene_enriched_in as ND-only one-vs-rest enrichment evidence (NOT A MARKER) for a gene in a cell type, with expression support filters. Report cell_type_label, condition, comparison, effect_direction, rank_in_cell_type, log2FoldChange, padj, expression_call, confidence_label, expression_support_rule, thresholds, data_version, and data_source. Treat it as marker/enrichment support, not exclusive expression or causal function. Strong endocrine hormone markers in non-cognate cell types should be flagged as possible ambient RNA or mixed-cell artefact unless independently validated.
edge_skill.OCR_locate_in: PanKgraph currently uses a single per-gene activity score as a placeholder OCR node, so each gene has only one OCR entry. This does not represent true OCR peak-level data. Until real OCR peaks are integrated, do not interpret OCR count per gene. Only report the gene activity score, and explicitly warn that the current OCR layer is a simplified proxy.
edge_skill.gene_activity_score_in: Interpret gene_activity_score_in as scATAC-seq-derived gene activity score in an anatomical structure or cell type. This is chromatin accessibility-derived gene activity, not RNA expression and not direct transcription rate. Report OCR_GeneActivityScore_mean and OCR_GeneActivityScore_median overall and by disease status when present. Avoid saying a gene is expressed from this edge alone; use phrasing such as accessibility-derived gene activity signal. Cross-condition differences are descriptive unless statistical testing is explicitly encoded.
edge_skill.OCR_peak_in: Interpret OCR_peak_in as an open chromatin region observed in or assigned to an anatomical structure or cell type. Unlike the old placeholder OCR node guidance, this edge points from a peak-level OCR_peak/regulatory_elements node to context. Report chr, start_loc, end_loc from the OCR node and data_source/description from the edge when present. Treat it as regulatory accessibility context, not proof that the linked region regulates a specific gene unless a separate regulatory link or functional evidence is present.
edge_skill.effector_gene_of;: Interpret effector_gene_of as a CMDKP/HuGeAMP-style prioritized mapping from Type 1 Diabetes evidence to candidate effector gene(s), not definitive mechanistic causality. Parse evidence as supporting evidence classes and sources when possible; report effector_gene_list_url, data_source_url, data_version, and data_source. Avoid treating the disease-gene edge as proof that the gene causes T1D without convergent fine-mapping, perturbation, or functional validation.
edge_skill.physical_interaction: Interpret physical_interaction as evidence of protein-level interaction under a specific assay context. Always report experimental_system, experimental_system_type, throughput, and qualifications; avoid assuming interaction strength, direction, or disease relevance unless explicitly encoded.
edge_skill.genetic_interaction: Interpret genetic_interaction as functional dependency/modification evidence, not direct physical binding. Keep assay context explicit and avoid causal direction claims unless a signed effect is provided.
edge_skill.function_annotation: Interpret function_annotation edges as ontology-based annotation links (membership/context), not proof of mechanism or disease causality.
edge_skill.fGSEA_enriched_in: Interpret fGSEA_enriched_in as pathway-level enrichment in a target anatomical structure or cell type from fGSEA. Report pathway_collection, pathway_term/name, cell_type_label, NES, ES, pval, padj, size, leadingEdge, source_file, data_version, and data_source. NES direction reflects enrichment direction in the ranked statistic, not necessarily upregulation of every pathway gene. Do not convert enrichment into causality or pathway activation without explaining the ranking contrast and supporting evidence.
edge_skill.marker_gene_of: Interpret marker_gene_of as external HuBMAP marker-gene annotation for a cell type. Report cell_type_name, gene_symbol, dataset_source, data_version, and source_row when present. Treat it as reference marker support, not PanKgraph differential expression evidence and not proof of exclusivity.
edge_skill.part_of_GWAS_signal: Interpret part_of_GWAS_signal as statistical locus membership (LD/credible-signal context), not proof that the variant is causal. Keep effect/non-effect alleles, method, and genome-build/version context explicit.
edge_skill.signal_COLOC_with: Interpret signal_COLOC_with as colocalization evidence of potentially shared association signal between QTL/GWAS credible sets. Coloc only responseble for the QTL/GWAS lead snp. You may find many QTL/ GWAS signals/ edge, but only the one clrearly stated in coloc edges are really coloc
edge_skill.part_of_QTL_signal: Interpret part_of_QTL_signal as statistical inclusion in a QTL signal/credible set for a specific tissue/context. Do not claim direct regulatory causality for a target gene without convergent evidence. Report QTL class/source when available through data_source (for example eQTL, sQTL, exonQTL, GTEx, INSPIRE), tissue_name, credible_set, pip, nominal_p, lbf, effect_allele, other_allele, slope, n_snp, purity, and data_version.

node_skill.coding_elements;gene: When describing a gene node, prioritize stable identifiers (HGNC symbol, Ensembl Gene ID) and clearly separate gene-level facts from dataset-derived signals.
node_skill.variants;sequence_variant;: When describing a sequence variant node, report the stable variant ID, chr, start_loc, end_loc, ref, alt, type, data_version, and data_source. Treat dbSNP/variant annotation flags as genomic annotation context, not disease causality. Causality requires supporting GWAS/QTL fine-mapping, colocalization, or functional validation edges.
node_skill.OCR_peak: When describing an OCR_peak/regulatory_elements node, report peak ID, chr, start_loc, end_loc, data_source, and type. Treat it as a peak-level open chromatin region. Do not infer target gene, enhancer/promoter function, or regulatory effect unless additional edges or annotations establish that link.PanKgraph currently uses limited OCR peaks from PanKbase snATACseq data. More statistics will coming in future updates
node_skill.gene_ontology: When describing a GO node, report stable GO ID + term name and treat it as functional vocabulary context. Do not convert term membership into a direct mechanistic claim without supporting evidence.
node_skill.kegg: When describing a KEGG pathway node, report KEGG ID, pathway name, link, and data_version. Treat it as pathway vocabulary/context; pathway membership alone is not pathway activation, enrichment, or disease causality.
node_skill.reactome: When describing a Reactome pathway node, report Reactome ID, pathway name, link, and data_version. Treat it as pathway vocabulary/context; pathway membership alone is not pathway activation, enrichment, or disease causality.
node_skill.anatomical_structure: When describing an anatomical_structure node, report category, name, source, source_url, and description. Treat it as anatomical/cell-type metadata context. Do not infer gene expression, disease involvement, or sample availability unless linked by the relevant molecular or metadata edge.
node_skill.Sample node: When describing a Sample node, report Data Modality, anatomical_structure, note, data_source, and contact when present. Treat samples as provenance records. Do not infer donor-level disease status or molecular findings from a sample node alone without has_sample/has_donor and molecular evidence.
node_skill.donor: When describing a donor node, report stable donor IDs and clinically relevant metadata such as derived_diabetes_status, diabetes_type, t1d_stage, aab_state, hba1c_percentage, c_peptide_ng_ml, age, sex_at_birth, Race, hla_status, data_source, and data_source_url when present. Treat donor fields as clinical/provenance metadata; flag missing, source-note, or conflicting values rather than forcing a single interpretation.
node_skill.donor;provenance: When describing a donor/provenance node, report stable donor IDs and clinically relevant metadata such as derived_diabetes_status, diabetes_type, t1d_stage, aab_state, hba1c_percentage, c_peptide_ng_ml, age, sex_at_birth, Race, hla_status, data_source, and data_source_url when present. Treat donor fields as clinical/provenance metadata; flag missing, source-note, or conflicting values rather than forcing a single interpretation.
node_skill.data_modality: When describing a data_modality node, treat it as assay or measurement context. Use it to clarify whether evidence comes from scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, bulk assays, BCR/TCR-seq, or other modalities; do not convert modality membership into a biological result.

complex_skill.DEG_in#expression_level_in#OCR_activity_: When interpreting a subgraph that includes DEG_in +/ expression_level_in +/ OCR_activity_in +/ OCR_locate_in, treat these as MULTI-MODAL signals and never summarize them as if they come from the same measurement. Enforce strict modality separation and provenance: (1) RNA differential expression (DEG_in) describes change in RNA abundance between conditions (e.g., T1D vs ND) within a specified cell type and analysis design (pseudobulk vs cell-level); report log2FC direction and padj, and state the cell type explicitly. (2) RNA expression_level_in describes within-condition expression summaries (mean/median/percent detected) and can be biased by ambient RNA, doublets, pseudobulk thresholds, donor imbalance, and normalization; avoid absolute presence/absence claims, and flag non-cognate hormone signals as likely artefacts unless supported by literature. (3) OCR_activity_in is chromatin accessibility / gene-activity derived from ATAC/OCR and is NOT RNA expression; never call OCR activity 'expression counts' or 'expression data'. (4) OCR_locate_in indicates genomic/regulatory localization of OCRs (e.g., enhancer/promoter regions) and supports regulatory context, not transcript abundance. If RNA indicates upregulation while OCR activity decreases (or vice versa), do NOT label as a contradiction; present as 'discordant cross-modality signals' and give cautious interpretations: possible regulatory layer differences, timing, cell-state shifts, gene-activity scoring limitations, or sample composition differences. Always output a 4-line structured summary: (A) Cell type context used for ALL stats (or explicitly mark if mixed/unspecified), (B) RNA-DE result (log2FC, padj, direction), (C) RNA-expression summary (within-condition stats; artefact caveats), (D) ATAC/OCR result (activity stats + OCR locations), followed by a single sentence: 'These metrics measure different layers and need not match in direction.' Never infer causality (e.g., 'repressed by chromatin closing') unless supported by explicit regulatory evidence (e.g., OCR overlaps promoter/enhancer + consistent TF motif/activity + replicated pattern).
complex_skill.T1D_DEG_in#gene_detected_in#gene_activit: When interpreting a subgraph that includes T1D_DEG_in plus gene_detected_in, gene_activity_score_in, or OCR_peak_in, treat these as multi-modal and provenance-specific signals. Keep four layers separate: (A) cell type/anatomical context, (B) RNA differential expression in T1D with Log2FoldChange and Adjusted_P_value, (C) RNA detection/enrichment support with logCPM and percent-cell thresholds plus ambient/doublet caveats, and (D) ATAC/OCR gene activity or peak accessibility, explicitly labeled as chromatin accessibility-derived evidence. Discordant RNA and ATAC signals are not contradictions by themselves. Do not infer regulatory causality without explicit regulatory links or validation.
complex_skill.part_of_QTL_signal#part_of_GWAS_signal#s: When interpreting a genetics-to-gene-to-disease subgraph containing QTL, GWAS, colocalization, and effector-gene edges, separate statistical locus membership, QTL target association, colocalization evidence, and curated/predicted effector-gene evidence. Report PIP, credible set, alleles, tissue, PP.H4.abf, GWAS/QTL signal IDs, evidence sources, and versions when present. Strong language such as causal variant, causal gene, or mechanism requires convergent high-confidence evidence and should otherwise be phrased as prioritized candidate or shared-signal evidence.
complex_skill.pathway_annotation;KEGG#pathway_annotati: When interpreting ontology/pathway subgraphs, separate static annotation membership from enrichment results. GO/KEGG/Reactome annotation says a gene belongs to a term/pathway; fGSEA_enriched_in says a pathway was enriched in a ranked analysis for a context. Report term IDs/names, NES, padj, leadingEdge, pathway_collection, and cell_type_label. Do not infer pathway activation, suppression, or disease causality unless the ranking direction and supporting molecular evidence are explicit.
